title: Synchronization for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
problem: Logical qubits encoded with the surface code in fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) can become desynchronized across their syndrome generation cycles due to heterogeneous QEC codes (color, qLDPC), fabrication defects causing extended clock cycles, and modular chip-to-chip coupling latencies. Lattice Surgery merge operations require all involved patches to begin their next syndrome generation cycle in lockstep, so desynchronized patches must idle—accumulating decoherence errors—before the operation can proceed.
motivation: Idling errors during forced synchronization are one of the primary causes of logical failures in current FTQC experiments (Google reports idling as the second-highest error contributor even with dynamical decoupling), and 1–11 synchronization events occur per error-correction cycle across practical workloads, making this bottleneck unavoidable at scale.
method: In fault-tolerant quantum computers, logical qubits (bits encoded across many physical qubits for error correction) sometimes run at different speeds and must synchronize before merging via Lattice Surgery (a qubit-merging operation). This paper proposes three synchronization strategies: Passive idles the fast qubits for their entire time deficit right before the merge—one long wait that lets decoherence errors build up; Active spreads this idle time into small chunks inserted after each error-correction round, preventing long waits; and Hybrid runs extra error-correction rounds on slower qubits to shrink the time deficit, then applies Active to the remainder. A hardware controller (Patch Counter Table, Phase Calculators, and Synchronization Slack Calculator) tracks when each qubit region finishes its cycles and injects timing directives into the control schedule without adding latency.
key_novelty: Active synchronization distributes idle time across multiple error-correction rounds rather than all at once, reducing peak decoherence per round and cutting the logical error rate by up to 3.4x.
contributions: Characterization of desynchronization sources in heterogeneous FTQC systems (mixed QEC codes, dropouts, modular architectures) and quantification of synchronization frequency across real workloads.
Active synchronization policy that distributes slack across multiple syndrome rounds, reducing logical error rate by up to 2.4x vs. Passive.
Hybrid policy combining extra-round correction with Active synchronization, reducing LER by up to 3.4x and decoding latency by up to 2.2x.
Open-source stabilizer circuit simulator integrated with Stim for evaluating surface-code Lattice Surgery synchronization policies.

metrics.speedup: 2.2x reduction in decoding latency (Hybrid vs. Passive)
metrics.accuracy: 3.4x reduction in logical error rate (Hybrid vs. Passive); 2.4x reduction (Active vs. Passive)
metrics.other: Validated on IBM Brisbane 127-qubit and IBM Sherbrooke quantum hardware

baselines: Passive synchronization (leading qubit idles for full slack)
limitations: Evaluations restricted to patch-based surface code and Lattice Surgery; generalization to color codes and qLDPC codes is discussed conceptually but not fully evaluated.
primary_theme: Logical qubit synchronization policies for fault-tolerant quantum computing
